arxiv-2206-03204.title: Isoperimetric problems for zonotopes Thanks: Partially supported by the BME Water Sciences & Disaster Prevention TKP2020 Institution Excellence Subprogram, grant no. TKP2020 BME-IKA-VIZ and the NKFIH grant K134199.
arxiv-2206-03204.creator: Antal Joós, Zsolt Lángi
arxiv-2206-03204.description: Abstract . Shephard (Canad. J. Math. 26: 302-321, 1974) proved a decomposition theorem for zonotopes yielding a simple formula for their volume. In this note we prove a generalization of this theorem yielding similar formulas for their intrinsic volumes. We use this result to investigate geometric extremum problems for zonotopes generated by a given number of segments.

arxiv-2210-00352.creator: M. Ghasemi 1 , A.A. Talebi 2 and N. Mehdipoor 3
arxiv-2210-00352.description: Abstract . Let s s be a positive integer. A graph is s s -transitive if its automorphism group is transitive on s-arcs but not on ( s + 1 ) (s+1) -arcs. In this paper, we study all tetravalent s s -transitive graphs of order 6 ​ p 2 6p^{2} . 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification 20B25, 05C25 1.

arxiv-2212-01692.title: Can In-context Learners Learn a Reasoning Concept from Demonstrations?
arxiv-2212-01692.creator: Michal Štefánik, Marek Kadlčík
arxiv-2212-01692.description: Abstract Language models exhibit an emergent ability to learn a new task from a small number of input-output demonstrations. However, recent work shows that in-context learners largely rely on their pre-trained knowledge, such as the sentiment of the labels, instead of learning new associations from the input.

arxiv-2304-13879.title: Emerton–Gee stacks, Serre weights, and Breuil–Mézard conjectures for GSp 4 \mathrm{GSp}_{4}

arxiv-2306-01258.creator: Jia Tian
arxiv-2306-01258.description: Abstract In this work, we study the holographic dual of the T T ¯ \overline{\text{T}} deformation following the mixed boundary condition proposal. We point out that a boundary term should be included in the gravity action in the holographic dictionary.

arxiv-2312-16420.title: NICER views moderate, strong, and extreme photospheric expansion bursts from the ultracompact X-ray binary 4U 1820–30 Preprint: Z. Li

arxiv-2312-16420.description: Abstract Type I X-ray bursts in the ultracompact X-ray binary 4U 1820–30 are powered by the unstable thermonuclear burning of hydrogen-deficient material. We report the detection of 15 type I X-ray bursts from 4U 1820–30 observed by NICER between 2017 and 2023. All these bursts occurred in the low state for the persistent flux in the range of 2.

arxiv-2412-07289.title: Enhancing Relation Extraction via Supervised Rationale Verification and Feedback
arxiv-2412-07289.creator: Yongqi Li, Xin Miao, Shen Zhou, Mayi Xu, Yuyang Ren, Tieyun Qian
arxiv-2412-07289.description: Abstract Despite the rapid progress that existing automated feedback methods have made in correcting the output of large language models (LLMs), these methods cannot be well applied to the relation extraction (RE) task due to their designated feedback objectives and correction manner.

arxiv-2502-01454.description: Abstract The string-net model describes a vast family of topological orders in two spatial dimensions. Here, we consider the effect of thermal fluctuations on these topological phases. In the original string-net model, the description of charge (vertex) excitations can be problematic. arxiv-2510-04027.title: Multi-Class Support Vector Machine with Differential Privacy
arxiv-2510-04027.creator: Jinseong Park, Yujin Choi, Jaewook Lee
arxiv-2510-04027.description: Abstract With the increasing need to safeguard data privacy in machine learning models, differential privacy (DP) is one of the major frameworks to build privacy-preserving models. Support Vector Machines (SVMs) are widely used traditional machine learning models due to their robust margin guarantees and strong empirical performance in binary classification.

arxiv-2511-11419.title: Regularized Black Hole Solution from a New String Cloud Source
arxiv-2511-11419.creator: Celio R. Muniz, Jonathan Alves Rebouças, Leonardo Tavares de Oliveira, Francisco Tiago Barboza Sampaio, Francisco Bento Lustosa
arxiv-2511-11419.description: Abstract We construct a new family of regular black hole solutions supported by the novel Letelier-Alencar string cloud and regularize it through a rational Dagum-type distribution. The regulator smooths the matter profile and ensures finite curvature invariants, yielding a geometry that interpolates between a string-cloud exterior and an anti-de Sitter core.

Although there are many human vaccines that contain multip

pmc-10744103.title: Sleep and Postpartum Psychosis: A Narrative Review of the Existing Literature
pmc-10744103.creator: Camilla Carr, Daniela Borges, Katie Lewis, Jessica Heron, Sally Wilson, Matthew R. Broome, Ian Jones, Arianna Di Florio, Isabel Morales-Muñoz
pmc-10744103.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Sleep problems are extremely common during the postpartum period. The role of sleep in the development of postpartum psychosis (PP) is, however, still under-researched. This narrative review aims to (1) provide a summary of the existing evidence for the associations between sleep problems and PP, (2) discuss the relevant risk factors associated with sleep problems and PP, and (3) suggest future lines of research in this area.

pmc-11591612.title: Integrating Historical Learning and Multi-View Attention with Hierarchical Feature Fusion for Robotic Manipulation
pmc-11591612.creator: Gaoxiong Lu, Zeyu Yan, Jianing Luo, Wei Li, Junzhi Yu
pmc-11591612.description: Humans typically make decisions based on past experiences and observations, while in the field of robotic manipulation, the robot’s action prediction often relies solely on current observations, which tends to make robots overlook environmental changes or become ineffective when current observations are suboptimal.

pmc-12414804.title: PAPSS2‐Related Brachyolmia: Clinical and Radiographic Features and Growth Hormone Therapy of One Chinese Case
pmc-12414804.creator: Wenjun Long, Xiaoping Luo
pmc-12414804.description: Brachyolmia type 4 (BCYM4, OMIM 612847) is a rare skeletal dysplasia characterized by mild epiphyseal and metaphyseal abnormalities. We report a Chinese boy with brachyolmia caused by a novel compound heterozygous mutation in the PAPSS2 gene. Prenatal ultrasound revealed shortened long bones, and his birth length was markedly reduced (45 cm, −3.11 SD).

pmc-12642157.title: Effectiveness of a psychoeducational intervention for people with suicidal behavior in the prison environment. N’VIU project: a randomized control trial
pmc-12642157.creator: Quintí Foguet-Boreu, Manel Capdevila-Capdevila, Judit Pons-Baños, Lola Riesco- Miranda, Ana Sanjuan Torres, Marian Martínez García, Berta Framis-Ferrer, Saray Valdivieso Muñoz
pmc-12642157.description: BackgroundSuicide rates are higher in prison environments than those in the general population. Therefore, preventive activities are crucial. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a psychoeducational group intervention in decreasing the number of suicidal behaviors in prisons.MethodsWe conducted a randomized controlled trial in nine prisons in Catalonia. Main outcome: total number of suicidal behaviors.

pmc-12755110.title: Targeted-Immunomodulatory Nanomedicines for the Treatment of Autoimmune Diseases via Multiple Administration Routes
pmc-12755110.creator: Bom Lee, Jeeeun Yoo, Han Sol Lee, Yonghyun Lee
pmc-12755110.description: The incidence and prevalence of autoimmune diseases are rising globally, presenting a significant health challenge. Current treatments focus on symptom management and immunosuppression, often resulting in side-effects such as increased infection risk and broad immunosuppression. Targeted immune modulation strategies, particularly through nanomedicines, offer promising advancements by enabling precise drug delivery and reducing systemic toxicity, risks, and pharmacokinetic issues.

pmc-13043562.title: Characterization and Antifungal Activity of Essential oil of Cymbopogon citratus: Special Emphasis on Preliminary Fungicidal Mechanisms against Candida auris and Cryptococcus neoformans
pmc-13043562.creator: Lívia Gurgel do Amaral Valente Sá, Islay Lima Magalhães, Bruno Coêlho Cavalcanti, Álvaro Gabriel De Souza Araújo, Marcos Vinicius Queiroz Ambrósio Correia, Thaís Lima Ferreira, Daniel Sampaio Rodrigues, Vitória Pessoa de Farias Cabral, Lara Elloyse Almeida Moreira Gomes, Leilson Carvalho de Oliveira
pmc-13043562.description: In 2022, the World Health Organization published a list highlighting Candida auris and Cryptococcus neoformans as among the priority pathogens in need of new therapeutic alternatives. The essential oil of Cymbopogon citratus (EOCC) is used in folk medicine for its various properties, including antimicrobial activity.

pmc-13146584.title: Critical care access and outcomes in residents of inpatient-care catchment areas with and without ICUs: a nationwide cohort study in Japan
pmc-13146584.creator: Hiroyuki Ohbe, Nobuaki Shime, Kei Nishiyama, Takuya Sato, Kent Doi, Kiyohide Fushimi, Hiroki Matsui, Hideo Yasunaga, Daisuke Kudo
pmc-13146584.description: SummaryBackgroundIn Japan, many secondary medical areas (SMAs), defined as regional self-sufficient inpatient-care planning units, are not equipped with intensive care unit (ICU) beds. We aimed to describe the national distribution of SMAs without ICUs, compared post-arrival outcomes among ICU-admitted patients, and evaluated ICU access and mortality among critically ill patients.

pmc-13202941.title: Predictors of work engagement and burnout among rural nurses in Japan during COVID-19: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13202941.creator: Yuri Kai, Maki Kanaoka, Aki Nozue, Sayaka Kato, Rinko Uchida, Ryuichiro Takeda, Yumiko Kinoshita
pmc-13202941.description: BackgroundWork engagement and burnout are distinct psychological constructs, yet their coexistence under prolonged crisis conditions remains insufficiently examined, particularly in rural healthcare settings. This study investigated predictors of both work engagement and burnout among nurses in rural Japan during the later phase of the COVID-19 pandemic (July 2022).
